items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: It’s one on which Earle Warren sang, but it had a solo in an introduction

ctx.x: Bobby Merrill was a – he was about ten years older than me. He was a marvelous trumpet player with a great big sound, and I’ll never forget him, because he was unusually kind to me. He used to – he was a working musician, and I was a scuffling kid, and he used to give me a couple of bucks every now and then, buy me a sandwich or something. He was just a nice person. He was a good singer. I’ll never forget the – one of the tunes that was very popular at that time was a Count Basie record of I struck a match in the…
